featureName: Household Profiles and Scoped Immich Credentials
summary: Permit each family member to use PhotoDesk through an authenticated household profile backed by that person's own user-scoped Immich API key. Review sessions, reviewed state, edits, and caches remain private to the profile even when Immich partner sharing makes household photos visible in a combined timeline.
productIntent: The household can share photos through Immich without forcing everyone to operate as the Immich administrator.
Each person gets an independent PhotoDesk workspace and can review the same shared photo independently.
Immich remains the authority for asset visibility and mutation permissions; PhotoDesk does not invent broader access.
Parents can provision, disable, and recover household profiles without gaining routine access to another person's plaintext API key.

recommendedDirection.identity: Use a PhotoDesk household profile and secure server-side session. Reuse the member/passphrase and parent/member role concepts already established in FamilyPulse and HomeSource unless the homeApps suite adopts a shared OIDC or trusted reverse-proxy identity layer first.
recommendedDirection.immichCredential: Map exactly one active Immich API key to each PhotoDesk profile. Validate it with Immich's current-user and current-key endpoints, record the Immich user ID and granted permissions, encrypt the secret at rest, and never return it to the browser after enrollment.
recommendedDirection.authorizationBoundary: Resolve the active PhotoDesk profile from its authenticated server session, then construct the Immich client from that profile's stored credential. Never accept a profile ID, Immich user ID, or credential selector from a normal API request.
recommendedDirection.reviewIsolation: Sessions and reviewed state are private per profile by default. The same Immich asset can therefore be reviewed by multiple family members without one person's commit removing it from another person's unreviewed queue.
recommendedDirection.sharedTimeline: Owned assets are the safest initial scope. Partner assets can be added as an opt-in read/discovery scope once ownership and endpoint capabilities are surfaced. A visible shared asset is not assumed to support rating, trash, stacking, editing, or derivative upload operations.
recommendedDirection.administration: A household admin can create or disable PhotoDesk profiles, inspect connection health and permission status, and request credential rotation. Plaintext API keys are write-only secrets.

rejectedDirections.option: One Immich administrator API key with a user picker in PhotoDesk
rejectedDirections.reason: The picker would be cosmetic authorization. Every request and write would still execute with administrator authority, making profile isolation fragile and audit trails misleading.

rejectedDirections.option: Store API keys in localStorage or send them with browser requests
rejectedDirections.reason: This exposes durable Immich credentials to browser storage, XSS, extensions, screenshots, and client logs.

rejectedDirections.option: Use Immich account passwords as PhotoDesk credentials
rejectedDirections.reason: PhotoDesk should not collect or retain Immich passwords. User-created API keys provide revocation and granular permission controls.
The stated use case requires each person to have their own sessions. Household-shared review state could be a later explicit collaboration mode, not the default.

currentSingleUserAssumptions.impact: One process-wide IMMICH_API_KEY and IMMICH_URL are used for every request.
Authentication headers are built from the global configuration rather than request/profile context.
Sessions have no owner/profile foreign key.
processed_assets uses asset_id as a global primary key, so one person's commit currently marks the asset reviewed for everyone.
There is one cached library snapshot and one global processed-asset set.

profiles: role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('household_admin', 'member'))
auth_subject TEXT or passphrase_hash TEXT, depending on the selected identity approach
status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('active', 'disabled'))
profile_sessions: Opaque random session token stored as a hash
HttpOnly, Secure in production, SameSite cookie
immich_credentials: key_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL for support and rotation without revealing the key
permissions TEXT NOT NULL as the last verified JSON snapshot
ownershipChanges: Add profile_id NOT NULL to sessions.
Change processed_assets identity from asset_id to UNIQUE(profile_id, asset_id), retaining session_id for provenance.
Partition density_cache by profile_id and library_scope instead of the singleton id=1 row.
Derive decisions, ratings, stacks, and edits through their owning session; direct profile_id columns are unnecessary unless profiling later proves joins costly.
Record library_scope on sessions and cached snapshots, initially 'owned' and later optionally 'owned_and_partners'.
proposedDataModel.migration: Create one household_admin profile for the existing installation, attach all existing sessions and reviewed state to it, move the current environment API key into the credential enrollment path, and preserve all current data. The migration must be transactional and represented in db/migrations plus db/schema.sql.

credentialSecurity: Require a PhotoDesk master encryption key from deployment secrets; fail closed rather than storing new Immich keys unencrypted.
Use authenticated encryption with a unique nonce per credential and bind ciphertext to the profile ID as additional authenticated data.
Redact x-api-key, session cookies, encrypted values, and submitted credentials from request and error logs.
Display only the key name/fingerprint, Immich account identity, granted capabilities, and last verification time after enrollment.
Allow credential replacement and profile disablement without affecting other profiles.
Use least-privilege Immich keys. The exact permission template must be generated from the endpoints PhotoDesk actually uses and updated as features change.
libraryAndCommitRules: The active profile's Immich key determines the assets visible to PhotoDesk.
Owned-library discovery and review should ship before partner-aware writes.
If partner assets are enabled, label asset ownership in discovery, workspace, editor, and commit summary.
Compute commit actions per asset from both API-key permissions and asset ownership/capability evidence.
Disable unsupported actions before commit and explain why; do not rely on an Immich 403 after the user finishes a session.

Rendered derivatives upload into the active Immich user's account. Do not stack a derivative with a partner-owned original until that behavior is verified against the deployed Immich version and product semantics are approved.
Cache keys and background refresh jobs must include profile_id and library_scope.

deliverySlices.name: Compatibility and threat-model spike
deliverySlices.outcome: Document the deployed Immich version, required API-key permission set, current-user/key verification calls, partner timeline retrieval, asset ownership fields, and mutation behavior for partner-owned assets.
exitCriteria: Two disposable Immich users and partner sharing are represented in integration fixtures or a reproducible local test setup.
Every PhotoDesk Immich endpoint is mapped to its required API-key permission.
Owned versus partner-owned write behavior is tested rather than inferred.

deliverySlices.name: Authenticated household profiles
deliverySlices.outcome: Add profile login/session management, parent/admin provisioning, encrypted per-profile credentials, and a migration of the existing installation to one admin profile.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Owned Immich library only; existing PhotoDesk workflows otherwise remain unchanged.

deliverySlices.name: Per-profile PhotoDesk state
deliverySlices.outcome: Partition sessions, reviewed assets, discovery snapshots, recent sessions, edits, and commits by profile.

deliverySlices.name: Partner timeline discovery
deliverySlices.outcome: Offer an explicit per-profile owned/partner timeline scope, show ownership badges, and keep unsupported mutations disabled.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Read/discovery first; commit support is capability-gated.

deliverySlices.name: Capability-aware shared workflows
deliverySlices.outcome: Enable only the partner/shared-asset operations proven safe and supported by Immich, with clear commit previews and audit records.
deliverySlices.scopeLimit: Do not broaden permissions through an administrator credential.

acceptanceCriteria: Profile A cannot list, retrieve, mutate, or infer Profile B's PhotoDesk sessions, decisions, ratings, edits, caches, or credentials.
The same Immich asset can be reviewed independently by two profiles and remains unreviewed for Profile B after Profile A commits it.
No normal browser request can choose another profile's Immich credential through a path, query, header, or request body value.
API keys are encrypted at rest, redacted from logs, never returned after enrollment, and independently replaceable or revocable.
PhotoDesk verifies and records the Immich user identity and permissions associated with each submitted key.
A disabled profile immediately loses PhotoDesk access without disrupting other household members.
Discovery and density caches are isolated by profile and selected library scope.
Shared partner assets are visibly distinguished from owned assets before review and commit.
Unsupported writes to partner-owned assets are prevented and explained before commit.
The existing single-user database migrates to one household administrator profile without losing sessions, reviewed state, edits, or commit history.
Automated tests cover two profiles with overlapping visible asset IDs and prove state isolation.
Browser tests cover profile switching, session isolation, credential rotation failure, and mobile login/session behavior.

openDecisions.recommendation: Start with the existing homeApps household member/passphrase pattern if this feature arrives before shared suite authentication. Prefer shared OIDC/reverse-proxy identity if the suite adopts it first.
openDecisions.whyOpen: This affects all homeApps and should not be decided accidentally inside PhotoDesk.

openDecisions.recommendation: Default to the active user's owned library; make partner timeline inclusion explicit.
openDecisions.whyOpen: The household wants a shared timeline, but shared visibility and safe commit rights are different concepts.

openDecisions.recommendation: Household admins may disable/reset a PhotoDesk profile, but API-key enrollment should still use the child's own Immich key and show who owns it.
openDecisions.whyOpen: The desired balance between parental administration and private review history has not been specified.

openDecisions.recommendation: Keep private review state as the invariant. Consider a separate named household queue only after individual workflows are proven.
openDecisions.whyOpen: A shared queue could be useful for the administrator's large library but would change the meaning of 'reviewed'.

researchReferences.title: Immich API authentication
researchReferences.finding: API keys are user-scoped and sent with the x-api-key header.

researchReferences.title: Create an Immich API key
researchReferences.finding: Keys can be limited to specified permissions.

researchReferences.title: Get current Immich user
researchReferences.finding: PhotoDesk can verify the user identity represented by a submitted credential.

researchReferences.title: Get current Immich API key
researchReferences.finding: PhotoDesk can inspect the key currently authenticating a request and its granted permissions.

researchReferences.title: Immich partner sharing
researchReferences.finding: Partner sharing is one-way, may be integrated into the timeline per partner, and shares broad asset metadata while excluding some user-specific information.

researchReferences.title: Immich timeline buckets
researchReferences.finding: Timeline retrieval exposes a withPartners option suitable for a future partner-aware discovery spike.

researchReferences.title: Immich OAuth configuration
researchReferences.finding: Immich acts as an OIDC client to an external identity provider. A suite-wide identity provider could authenticate both Immich and PhotoDesk, but Immich itself should not be assumed to be PhotoDesk's OAuth provider.
